artworks.title: View of Burning Troy
artworks.description: Trautmann's blazing Troy — the night Virgil names when neighbouring Ucalegon's house already burns, the Trojan counsellor who became a proverb for the neighbour whose roof is on fire.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Book II — as Troy falls, Aeneas sees Ucalegon's house already in flames: iam proximus ardet Ucalegon — the line that made a minor Trojan elder a European proverb for imminent danger next door.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book III — Ucalegon sits among Priam's elders on the wall, watching Helen: a counsellor of Troy before Virgil's fire made his name proverbial.

popCulture.title: Ucalegon
popCulture.description: Trojan elder whose burning house in the Aeneid became a byword — 'Ucalegon next door' for a neighbour already ablaze.
